sections.overview: Parectropis similaria is a European geometrid moth associated with broad-leaved woodland.
sections.identification: The adult has densely mottled, brindled wings with a conspicuous pale patch near the outer forewing. Its wingspan is about 33–39 mm.
sections.habitat: It is recorded from much of Europe and locally favours deciduous or ancient woodland; records also come from gardens near wooded landscapes.
sections.diet: The caterpillars feed on leaves of oaks, birches, hazel and hawthorn; recorded host lists vary by region.
sections.behavior: Adults are mainly on the wing from late May into early July in southern Britain and are attracted to light; local flight periods can vary.
sections.reproduction: In the British account, the species is single-brooded and winters as a pupa.
sections.ecology: Its larvae use several common deciduous trees and shrubs, linking the moth to structurally varied woodland edges and broad-leaved habitats.
sections.conservation: Regional records show a local rather than uniformly abundant moth; the sources consulted do not provide a global conservation assessment.
